claim: Obesity induced by high-fat diet (HFD) is a multi-factorial disease including genetic, physiological, behavioral, and environmental components.
source: Obesity induced by high-fat diet (HFD) is a multi-factorial disease including genetic, physiological, behavioral, and environmental components.
evidence: This is a general statement about obesity that draws from established scientific understanding of the disease.

claim: Drosophila has emerged as an effective metabolic disease model.
source: Drosophila has emerged as an effective metabolic disease model.
evidence: This statement reflects established scientific consensus about Drosophila as a model organism.

claim: Cytidine 5'-triphosphate synthase (CTPS) is an important enzyme for the de novo synthesis of CTP, governing the cellular level of CTP and the rate of phospholipid synthesis.
source: Cytidine 5'-triphosphate synthase (CTPS) is an important enzyme for the de novo synthesis of CTP, governing the cellular level of CTP and the rate of phospholipid synthesis.
evidence: This statement describes the established biochemical function of CTPS.

claim: CTPS is known to form filamentous structures called cytoophidia, which are found in bacteria, archaea, and eukaryotes.
source: CTPS is known to form filamentous structures called cytoophidia, which are found in bacteria, archaea, and eukaryotes.
evidence: This statement references established knowledge about CTPS structures across different domains of life.

claim: CTPS is crucial in regulating body weight and starvation resistance in Drosophila by functioning in the fat body.
source: Our study demonstrates that CTPS is crucial in regulating body weight and starvation resistance in Drosophila by functioning in the fat body.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: HFD-induced obesity leads to increased transcription of CTPS and elongates cytoophidia in larval adipocytes.
source: HFD-induced obesity leads to increased transcription of CTPS and elongates cytoophidia in larval adipocytes.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Depleting CTPS in the fat body prevented HFD-induced obesity, including body weight gain, adipocyte expansion, and lipid accumulation, by inhibiting the PI3K-Akt-SREBP axis.
source: Depleting CTPS in the fat body prevented HFD-induced obesity, including body weight gain, adipocyte expansion, and lipid accumulation, by inhibiting the PI3K-Akt-SREBP axis.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data presented in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: A dominant-negative form of CTPS also prevented adipocyte expansion and downregulated lipogenic genes.
source: Furthermore, a dominant-negative form of CTPS also prevented adipocyte expansion and downregulated lipogenic genes.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data presented in Figure 6.

claim: The consumption of high-fat diets (HFDs) is a leading contributor to obesity.
source: The consumption of high-fat diets (HFDs) is a leading contributor to obesity, a major risk factor for chronic disorders such as diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and cancer, responsible for approximately 2.5 million deaths yearly (Ogden et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Ogden et al., 2007.

claim: Obesity is a major risk factor for chronic disorders such as diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and cancer, responsible for approximately 2.5 million deaths yearly.
source: The consumption of high-fat diets (HFDs) is a leading contributor to obesity, a major risk factor for chronic disorders such as diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and cancer, responsible for approximately 2.5 million deaths yearly (Ogden et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Ogden et al., 2007.

claim: CTPS catalyzes the transfer of amide nitrogen from glutamine to the C-4 position of UTP, a process that requires ATP.
source: CTPS is a rate-limiting enzyme in the de novo synthesis of CTP, catalyzing the transfer of amide nitrogen from glutamine to the C-4 position of UTP, a process that requires ATP (Lieberman, 1955; Levitzki and Koshland, 1969).
evidence: This statement describes the enzymatic mechanism of CTPS and is supported by citations to Lieberman, 1955 and Levitzki and Koshland, 1969.

claim: CTPS could polymerize into filamentous structures, termed cytoophidia or CTPS filaments, first reported in 2010.
source: In 2010, our research group and others reported that CTPS could polymerize into filamentous structures, termed cytoophidia (Liu, 2010) or CTPS filaments (Ingerson-Mahar et al., 2010; Noree et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Liu, 2010; Ingerson-Mahar et al., 2010; and Noree et al., 2010.

claim: CTPS filamentous structures were observed in fruit flies, bacteria, and yeast cells.
source: These structures were observed in fruit flies (Liu, 2010), bacteria (Ingerson-Mahar et al., 2010), and yeast cells (Noree et al., 2010), and subsequent research demonstrated their presence in human cells (Chen et al., 2011; Carcamo et al., 2011), plants, and archaea (Daumann et al., 2018; Liu, 2011; Liu, 2016; Zhou et al., 2020), indicating that CTPS filamentation is a highly conserved process across prokaryotic and eukaryotic organisms.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to studies demonstrating CTPS structures in different organisms.

claim: CTPS filamentation is a highly conserved process across prokaryotic and eukaryotic organisms.
source: These structures were observed in fruit flies (Liu, 2010), bacteria (Ingerson-Mahar et al., 2010), and yeast cells (Noree et al., 2010), and subsequent research demonstrated their presence in human cells (Chen et al., 2011; Carcamo et al., 2011), plants, and archaea (Daumann et al., 2018; Liu, 2011; Liu, 2016; Zhou et al., 2020), indicating that CTPS filamentation is a highly conserved process across prokaryotic and eukaryotic organisms.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the observation of CTPS structures across multiple domains of life, supported by citations.

claim: CTPS cytoophidia have several functions, including modulation of enzymatic activity, maintenance of cell morphology, and stabilization of CTPS protein.
source: Various studies have revealed that CTPS cytoophidia have several functions, including modulation of enzymatic activity (Aughey et al., 2014; Aughey and Liu, 2015), maintenance of cell morphology (Ingerson-Mahar et al., 2010), and stabilization of CTPS protein (Liu, 2016; Sun and Liu, 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to studies investigating CTPS cytoophidia functions.

claim: CTPS cytoophidia have been found in several human cancers, including hepatocellular carcinoma.
source: Notably, CTPS cytoophidia have been found in several human cancers, including hepatocellular carcinoma (Chang et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Chang et al., 2017.

claim: Mammalian adipose or hepatic tissues produce a substantial amount of CTPS.
source: It is worth noting that mammalian adipose or hepatic tissues produce a substantial amount of CTPS.
evidence: This statement appears to be based on established knowledge about CTPS expression patterns.

claim: Drosophila has emerged as a powerful and simplified model of metabolic diseases such as HFD-induced obesity, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease.
source: Drosophila has emerged as a powerful and simplified model of metabolic diseases such as HFD-induced obesity, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease (Birse et al., 2010; Oldham, 2011; Liu et al., 2012; Smith et al., 2014) because it offers the opportunity to investigate the links between genetics, diet, and metabolism.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to studies using Drosophila as a metabolic disease model.

claim: CTPS cytoophidia are abundantly distributed in various tissues, including the central nervous system, fat body and intestine of Drosophila.
source: Our previous investigation revealed that CTPS cytoophidia are abundantly distributed in various tissues, including the central nervous system, fat body and intestine of Drosophila (Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2020, which appears to be a previous study by the authors.

claim: The Drosophila fat body plays a crucial role in sensing nutritional conditions and responding through the integration of lipid metabolism, acting as an equivalent to the mammalian liver or adipose tissue.
source: The Drosophila fat body, an organ with high metabolic activity and conserved signaling pathways, plays a crucial role in sensing nutritional conditions and responding through the integration of lipid metabolism, acting as an equivalent to the mammalian liver or adipose tissue (Li et al., 2019; Arrese and Soulages, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Li et al., 2019 and Arrese and Soulages, 2010.

claim: The single Drosophila ortholog of CTPS, which forms cytoophidia in larval adipocytes, promotes adipocyte adhesion mediated by integrin-Collagen IV.
source: Our recent research has revealed that the single Drosophila ortholog of CTPS, which forms cytoophidia in larval adipocytes, promotes adipocyte adhesion mediated by integrin-Collagen IV (Zhang et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Zhang et al., 2020 and Liu et al., 2022, which appear to be previous studies by the authors.

claim: Female flies in the TubG4ts>CTPS-Ri group weighed 16.4%, 14.4%, and 11.0% less than those in the TubG4ts>+, CTPS-Ri/+, and TubG4ts>Con-Ri groups, respectively.
source: Female flies in the TubG4ts>CTPS-Ri group (1.003 mg; S.E.M.: ±0.056 mg) weighed 16.4%, 14.4%, and 11.0% less than those in the TubG4ts> + (1.2 mg; S.E.M.: ±0.066 mg), CTPS-Ri/+ (1.172 mg; S.E.M.: ±0.079 mg), and TubG4ts>Con-Ri (1.127 mg; S.E.M.: ±0.020 mg) groups, respectively (Figure 1A).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1A.

claim: Male TubG4ts>CTPS-Ri flies weighed 9.8%, 9.1%, and 7.7% less than those in the TubG4ts>+, CTPS-Ri/+, and TubG4ts>Con-Ri groups, respectively.
source: Similarly, male TubG4ts>CTPS-Ri flies (0.745 mg; S.E.M.:±0.017 mg) weighed 9.8%, 9.1%, and 7.7% less than those in the TubG4ts>+ (0.826 mg; S.E.M.: ±0.017 mg), CTPS-Ri/+ (0.82 mg; S.E.M.: ±0.009 mg) and TubG4 ts>Con-Ri (0.807 mg; S.E.M.: ±0.065 mg) groups, respectively (Figure 1A).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1A.

claim: The body weights of female and male ElavG4>CTPS-Ri flies did not differ significantly from those of the corresponding ElavG4>+, CTPS-Ri/+, and ElavG4>Con-Ri control flies.
source: In contrast to the global knockdown flies, the body weights of female and male ElavG4>CTPS-Ri flies did not differ significantly from those of the corresponding ElavG4>+, CTPS-Ri/+, and ElavG4>Con-Ri control flies (Figure 1B).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1B.

claim: The body weight of the CgG4>CTPS-Ri female flies was 29%, 26.7%, and 22.4% less than those of the CgG4>+, CTPS-Ri/+, and CgG4>Con-Ri flies.
source: Specifically, the body weight of the CgG4>CTPS-Ri female flies (0.859 mg; S.E.M.: ±0.148 mg) was 29%, 26.7%, and 22.4% less than those of the CgG4>+ (1.21 mg; S.E.M.: ±0.026 mg), CTPS-Ri/+ (1.172 mg; S.E.M.: ±0.079 mg), and CgG4>Con-Ri (1.108 mg; S.E.M.:±0.134 mg) flies.
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1C.

claim: The body weight of the CgG4>CTPS-Ri male flies was 12.9%, 9.8%, and 10.8% less than those of the CgG4>+, CTPS-Ri/+, and CgG4>Con-Ri lines, respectively.
source: Similarly, the body weight of the CgG4>CTPS-Ri male flies (0.740 mg; S.E.M.: ±0.027 mg) was also significantly reduced: 12.9%, 9.8%, and 10.8% less than those of the CgG4>+ (0.85 mg; S.E.M.: ±0.027 mg), CTPS-Ri/+ (0.82 mg; S.E.M.: ±0.009 mg), and CgG4>Con-Ri (0.83 mg; S.E.M.: ±0.002 mg) lines, respectively (Figure 1C).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1C.

claim: The lower efficiency of CTPS knockdown in the entire body (33–44%) compared to the fat body (62–64%) may account for the weakened body weight loss observed in TubG4ts>CTPS-Ri flies.
source: The lower efficiency of CTPS knockdown in the entire body (33–44%) compared to the fat body (62–64%) (Figure 1D and F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,C) may account for the weakened body weight loss observed in TubG4ts>CTPS-Ri flies (Figure 1A and C).
evidence: This statement is an inference based on qRT-PCR data showing different knockdown efficiencies in different tissues.

claim: CTPS in the fat body is necessary to facilitate weight gain.
source: Conversely, even though CTPS knockdown was more pronounced in pan neuron cells (75–82%) than in the fat body (Figure 1E and F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C), this knockdown did not reduce body weight, indicating that CTPS in the fat body is necessary to facilitate weight gain.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on comparing the effects of CTPS knockdown in different tissues.

claim: Female and male TubG4ts>CTPS-Ri flies had considerably shorter survival durations when starved compared to control flies.
source: Our investigation aimed to determine the impact of CTPS on starvation response, and we found that female and male TubG4ts>CTPS-Ri flies had considerably shorter survival durations when starved. Specifically, when TubG4ts> CTPS-Ri flies were compared to TubG4ts>+, CTPS-Ri/+, and TubG4ts>Con-Ri flies, female median survival rates declined by 30.2%, 25%, and 40%, respectively, whereas male median survival rates fell by 50%, 20%, and 20%, respectively (Figure 1G).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1G.

claim: Female and male CgG4>CTPS-Ri flies showed reduced survival durations in starvation conditions when compared to CgG4>+, CTPS-Ri/+, and CgG4>Con-Ri flies.
source: Moreover, female and male CgG4>CTPS-Ri flies showed reduced survival durations in starvation conditions when compared to CgG4>+, CTPS-Ri/+, and CgG4>Con-Ri flies. Specifically, female median survival rates declined by 17.1%, 27.5%, and 42%, respectively, whereas male median survival rates decreased by 25%, 25%, and 25%, respectively (Figure 1I).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1I.

claim: Under adequate nutritional conditions, the TAG content of CgG4>CTPS-Ri flies was reduced by 74.1%, 83.5%, and 62.5% when compared to CgG4>+, CTPS-Ri/+, and CgG4>Con-Ri flies, respectively.
source: Under adequate nutritional conditions, the TAG content of CgG4>CTPS-Ri flies was reduced by 74.1%, 83.5%, and 62.5% when compared to CgG4>+, CTPS-Ri/+, and CgG4>Con-Ri flies, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: In CgG4>CTPS-Ri flies, TAG was almost completely depleted after 24 hour food deprivation.
source: The TAG levels in flies declined gradually when they were starved, and in CgG4>CTPS-Ri flies, TAG was almost completely depleted after 24 hour food deprivation (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claim: The lack of starvation resistance observed when CTPS is deficient may be due in part to inadequate TAG storage.
source: These results explain the lower median survival rate of CgG4>CTPS-Ri flies compared to the control lines (Figure 1I), and suggest that the lack of starvation resistance observed when CTPS is deficient may be due in part to inadequate TAG storage.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the correlation between reduced TAG levels and reduced starvation resistance.

claim: CTPS knockdown significantly decreased larval body weight when compared to that measured in CgG4>+, CTPS-Ri/+, and CgG4>Con-Ri control lines.
source: We observed that CTPS knockdown significantly decreased larval body weight when compared to that measured in CgG4>+, CTPS-Ri/+, and CgG4>Con-Ri control lines (Figure 2A), while having no effect on larval body size (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2A.

claim: CTPS knockdown had no effect on larval body size.
source: We observed that CTPS knockdown significantly decreased larval body weight when compared to that measured in CgG4>+, CTPS-Ri/+, and CgG4>Con-Ri control lines (Figure 2A), while having no effect on larval body size (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: 80% of CgG4>CTPS-Ri larvae sank to the bottom of the vial, whereas 80%–90% of the control larvae floated on top of the approximately 12% sugar solution.
source: Our results revealed that 80% of CgG4>CTPS-Ri larvae sank to the bottom of the vial, whereas 80%–90% of the control larvae floated on top of the approximately 12% sugar solution (Figure 2B).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2B.

claim: CTPS expression in the fat body is upregulated by 120% under HFD feeding compared to RD conditions.
source: Our results demonstrated that CTPS expression in the fat body is upregulated by 120% under HFD feeding compared to RD conditions (Figure 3A).
evidence: This statement is supported by qRT-PCR data presented in Figure 3A.

claim: The CTPS cytoophidia in the fat body of HFD-fed CTPS-mCh larvae were elongated by up to 60% when compared to those in RD-fed larvae.
source: In addition, we observed that the CTPS cytoophidia in the fat body of HFD-fed CTPS-mCh larvae were elongated by up to 60% (Figure 3B–D) when compared to those in RD-fed larvae, while cytoophidia numbers were also increased modestly (Figure 3E).
evidence: This statement is supported by confocal microscopy data presented in Figures 3B-D.

claim: Cytoophidia numbers were increased modestly in HFD-fed larvae compared to RD-fed larvae.
source: In addition, we observed that the CTPS cytoophidia in the fat body of HFD-fed CTPS-mCh larvae were elongated by up to 60% (Figure 3B–D) when compared to those in RD-fed larvae, while cytoophidia numbers were also increased modestly (Figure 3E).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data presented in Figure 3E.

claim: Elongated cytoophidia and elevated CTPS in the fat body may facilitate metabolic adaptation in response to a HFD.
source: These findings suggest that elongated cytoophidia and elevated CTPS in the fat body may facilitate metabolic adaptation in response to a HFD.
evidence: This statement is a speculation based on the observed changes in CTPS expression and cytoophidia morphology in response to HFD.

claim: CgG4>+ larvae fed HFD gained significantly more body weight (429%, 1.550 mg) than those on a RD (0.293 mg).
source: CgG4 >+ larvae fed HFD gained significantly more body weight (429%, 1.550 mg; S.E.M.: ±0.021 mg) than those on a RD (0.293 mg; S.E.M.: ±0.011 mg) (Figure 4B).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4B.

claim: HFD-fed CgG4>CTPS-Ri larvae exhibited a 64.6% decrease in body weight when compared to HFD-fed CgG4>+ larvae.
source: However, HFD-fed CgG4>CTPS-Ri larvae (0.549 mg; S.E.M.: ±0.096 mg) exhibited a 64.6% decrease in body weight when compared to HFD-fed CgG4>+ larvae (Figure 4B).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4B.

claim: CTPS knockdown resulted in a 73% reduction in body weight gain when compared to CgG4>+ larvae when both lines were fed HFD.
source: CTPS knockdown resulted in a 73% reduction in body weight gain when compared to CgG4>+ larvae when both lines were fed HFD (Figure 4B).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4B.

claim: In RD conditions, the TAG content of CgG4>CTPS-Ri larvae was 50%, 58.8%, and 55.4% lower than that of the CgG4>+, CTPS-Ri/+, or CgG4>CTPS-Ri control group, respectively.
source: In RD conditions, the TAG content of CgG4>CTPS-Ri larvae was 50%, 58.8%, and 55.4% lower than that of the CgG4>+, CTPS-Ri/+, or CgG4>CTPS-Ri control group, respectively (Figure 4E).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4E.

claim: Under HFD conditions, the TAG content in CgG4>CTPS-Ri larvae was 30.1%, 35%, and 31% lower than in the CgG4>+, CTPS-Ri/+, or CgG4>CTPS-Ri control groups, respectively.
source: Similarly, under HFD conditions, the TAG content in CgG4>CTPS-Ri larvae was 30.1%, 35%, and 31% lower than in the CgG4>+, CTPS-Ri/+, or CgG4>CTPS-Ri control groups, respectively (Figure 4E).
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4E.

claim: A remarkable reduction in HFD-induced adipocyte expansion was observed in CgG4>CTPS-Ri larvae, as evidenced by smaller cell and nuclear sizes than those in the control larvae.
source: In addition, we observed a remarkable reduction in HFD-induced adipocyte expansion in CgG4>CTPS-Ri larvae, as evidenced by smaller cell and nuclear sizes than those in the control larvae (Figure 4F–H).
evidence: This statement is supported by confocal microscopy data and quantification presented in Figures 4F-H.

claim: The clones expressing CTPS RNAi were considerably smaller than their control clones.
source: Remarkably, the clones expressing CTPS RNAi were considerably smaller than their control clones (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, B and C), indicating that CTPS is required for adipocytes to sustain growth cell-autonomously.
evidence: This statement is supported by clonal analysis data presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: CTPS is required for adipocytes to sustain growth cell-autonomously.
source: Remarkably, the clones expressing CTPS RNAi were considerably smaller than their control clones (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, B and C), indicating that CTPS is required for adipocytes to sustain growth cell-autonomously.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the clonal analysis showing smaller CTPS-deficient clones.

claim: The levels of the major phospholipids, including phosphatidylethanolamine (PE), phosphatidylcholine (PC), lysophosphatidylethanolamine (LPE), and lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC), were slightly reduced (although not significantly) when normalized to protein concentration in CTPS-deficient fat bodies.
source: We found that the levels of the major phospholipids, including phosphatidylethanolamine (PE), phosphatidylcholine (PC), lysophosphatidylethanolamine (LPE), and lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC), were slightly reduced (although not significantly) when normalized to protein concentration (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This statement is supported by lipidomic analysis data presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 3A.

claim: The expression of nmydn-D7 was increased in fat bodies expressing CTPS-Ri.
source: We found that the expression of nmydn-D7 was increased in fat bodies expressing CTPS-Ri (Figure 4—figure supplement 3B), indicating that fat bodies may upregulate nucleotide diphosphate kinase expression to compensate for CTP production when de novo CTP synthesis is hindered.
evidence: This statement is supported by qRT-PCR data presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Fat bodies may upregulate nucleotide diphosphate kinase expression to compensate for CTP production when de novo CTP synthesis is hindered.
source: We found that the expression of nmydn-D7 was increased in fat bodies expressing CTPS-Ri (Figure 4—figure supplement 3B), indicating that fat bodies may upregulate nucleotide diphosphate kinase expression to compensate for CTP production when de novo CTP synthesis is hindered.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the observed upregulation of nmydn-D7 in CTPS-deficient fat bodies.

claim: CTPS is essential for adipocyte expansion and lipogenesis in response to HFD consumption.
source: Taken together, our findings indicate that CTPS is essential for adipocyte expansion and lipogenesis in response to HFD consumption.
evidence: This statement is a conclusion based on multiple experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: RNA-Seq analysis identified 273 differentially expressed genes, with 204 genes (74.7%) upregulated and 69 genes (25.3%) downregulated in CTPS-deficient adipocytes compared to controls.
source: Our analysis identified 273 differentially expressed genes, with 204 genes (74.7%) upregulated and 69 genes (25.3%) downregulated in CTPS-deficient adipocytes compared to controls (≥2.0-fold change, Student's t-test, P<0.05) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This statement is supported by RNA-Seq data presented in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The differentially regulated genes were significantly enriched in lipid metabolism, carbohydrate metabolism, and amino acid metabolism.
source: Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analysis indicated that the differentially regulated genes were significantly enriched in lipid metabolism, carbohydrate metabolism, and amino acid metabolism (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This statement is supported by KEGG analysis data presented in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Downregulation of genes encoding lipogenic enzymes such as acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC) and fatty acid synthase 1 (FASN1) was observed in CTPS-deficient adipocytes.
source: Notably, we observed the downregulation of genes encoding lipogenic enzymes such as acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC) and fatty acid synthase 1 (FASN1), and of several other genes that are involved in lipid metabolism (Figure 5A).
evidence: This statement is supported by RNA-Seq data presented in Figure 5A.

claim: CTPS knockdown significantly decreased the expression levels of Acc and Fasn1 by 54–86.1% and 59–70.3%, respectively.
source: Our results showed that CTPS knockdown significantly decreased the expression levels of Acc and Fasn1 by 54–86.1% and 59–70.3%, respectively (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 2A, B).
evidence: This statement is supported by qRT-PCR data presented in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A, B.

claim: The expression levels of Srebp and Scap were reduced by 23–34.4% and 30–33.3%, respectively, in response to CTPS knockdown.
source: Our qRT-PCR results showed that the expression levels of Srebp and Scap were reduced by 23–34.4% and 30–33.3%, respectively, in response to CTPS knockdown (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This statement is supported by qRT-PCR data presented in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A, B.

claim: CTPS plays a role in regulating adipocyte lipogenesis by modulating the expression of lipogenic enzymes.
source: These findings suggest that CTPS plays a role in regulating adipocyte lipogenesis by modulating the expression of lipogenic enzymes.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the observed downregulation of lipogenic genes in CTPS-deficient adipocytes.

claim: A significant reduction in the cell membrane-associated tGPH signal was observed in the adipocytes of CgG4>CTPS-Ri.
source: When comparing the ratio of tGPH in the cell membrane to that in the cytosol, we observed a significant reduction in the cell membrane-associated tGPH signal in the adipocytes of CgG4>CTPS-Ri (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This statement is supported by confocal microscopy data and quantification presented in Figures 5C and D.

claim: When CTPS was knocked down, the expression level of Pi3K was not significantly reduced.
source: Our results demonstrated that when CTPS was knocked down, the expression level of Pi3K was not significantly reduced (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A), suggesting that CTPS depletion reduces PI3K activity rather than Pi3K expression level, which diminishes tGPH localization to the cell membrane.
evidence: This statement is supported by qRT-PCR data presented in Figure 5—figure supplement 3A.

claim: CTPS depletion reduces PI3K activity rather than Pi3K expression level, which diminishes tGPH localization to the cell membrane.
source: Our results demonstrated that when CTPS was knocked down, the expression level of Pi3K was not significantly reduced (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A), suggesting that CTPS depletion reduces PI3K activity rather than Pi3K expression level, which diminishes tGPH localization to the cell membrane.
evidence: This statement is an inference based on the observation that tGPH localization is reduced without a significant change in Pi3K expression.

claim: A significant decrease in the level of phosphorylated Akt was observed in the fat body of CgG4>CTPS-Ri larvae.
source: We observed a significant decrease in the level of phosphorylated Akt in the fat body of CgG4>CTPS-Ri larvae (Figure 5E).
evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data presented in Figure 5E.

claim: Overexpressing the truncated form of SREBP.Cdel partially rescued the reduction in adipocyte size and the smaller lipid droplet size caused by CTPS deficiency.
source: Intriguingly, we found that overexpressing the truncated form of SREBP.Cdel, constitutively activated and nuclear localized, partially rescued the reduction in adipocyte size and the smaller lipid droplet size caused by CTPS deficiency (Figure 5F and G).
evidence: This statement is supported by confocal microscopy data and quantification presented in Figures 5F and G.

claim: The TAG concentration was partially restored in larvae overexpressing SREBP.Cdel in the absence of CTPS, but did not reach the same level as that in the wild-type control.
source: Moreover, we observed that the TAG concentration was partially restored in larvae overexpressing SREBP.Cdel in the absence of CTPS, but did not reach the same level as that in the wild-type control (Figure 5H).
evidence: This statement is supported by TAG measurement data presented in Figure 5H.

claim: The overexpression of SREBP.Cdel alone led to a noteworthy reduction in both adipocyte and nuclear size, even though there was a marked increase in TAG accumulation.
source: It is important to highlight, however, that the overexpression of SREBP.Cdel alone led to a noteworthy reduction in both adipocyte and nuclear size, even though there was a marked increase in TAG accumulation.
evidence: This statement is an observation based on the experimental data.

claim: CTPS is crucial for the control of lipogenesis, potentially by preserving the activation of PI3K-Akt-SREBP signaling.
source: Collectively, our results suggest that CTPS is crucial for the control of lipogenesis, potentially by preserving the activation of PI3K-Akt-SREBP signaling.
evidence: This statement is a conclusion based on multiple experimental findings showing the effects of CTPS on PI3K-Akt-SREBP signaling.

claim: H355 in the domain of glutamine amidotransferase is critical for Drosophila cytoophidium formation.
source: Our research revealed that H355 in the domain of glutamine amidotransferase is critical for Drosophila cytoophidium formation (Zhou et al., 2019; Zhou et al., 2021a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Zhou et al., 2019 and Zhou et al., 2021a.

claim: CTPSMU-OE significantly reduced HFD-induced increases in body weight and TAG accumulation compared to the control lines.
source: CTPSMU-OE significantly reduced HFD-induced increases in body weight (Figure 6A and B) and TAG accumulation (Figure 6C) compared to the control lines.
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data presented in Figures 6A, B, and C.

claim: CTPSMU-OE resulted in body weight losses of 18.8%, 16.7%, and 18.8%, respectively, when compared to CgG4>+, CgG4>GFP, and CTPSMU/+ control lines.
